hero.eyebrow: Pallets move the world. We move pallets.
hero.heading: Never one mill between you and your line.
hero.body: AGL Pallet sources new, custom, and engineered pallets from a network of family-run mills across the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic — and manages the freight on every order. Same-day quotes. No minimums. More than one qualified source on every spec we sell.

cards.heading: Same-day quotes
cards.body: Send a spec and a quantity before lunch, get a number back the same day.

cards.heading: No minimums
cards.body: One truckload or forty. Order size doesn't decide whether we pick up the phone.

cards.heading: Freight on every order
cards.body: We book and track the truck. One number covers the pallets and the delivery.

whatWeDo.heading: One number for the spec, the pallets, and the truck.
paragraphs: AGL is a pallet brokerage. We don't own a mill and we don't own trucks. What we own is the coordination: we qualify the shops that build well, hold more than one source for every spec we quote, and book the freight so the pallets land when your line needs them.
When something moves — a spec change, a volume spike, a mill running behind — you hear it from us before it becomes your problem. That's the job.

cards.heading: You hear it from us first
cards.body: Proactive updates, not status requests. If a load slips, the call comes from us with the fix already in motion — not from your receiving dock at 6am.

cards.heading: More than one mill per spec
cards.body: Every spec we sell has multiple qualified shops behind it. No single facility, no single region, no single point of failure between a lumber market and your line.

cards.heading: We've run the floor
cards.body: AGL was built by people who bought pallets from the manufacturing side. We know which corners cost money later and which specs are overbuilt for the job.

pledge.heading: We will never own a mill.
paragraphs: After the COVID lumber shock, a lot of pallet brokers bought factories. Volume that had run through family mills for years quietly moved to the broker's own plants. It left both sides wary — mills don't trust a broker who competes with them, and buyers don't trust a broker who became a manufacturer.

AGL doesn't own manufacturing and has no intention of ever owning it. We grow by coordinating more, not by building plants. That's why good mills give us capacity, and it's why there's always more than one shop that can build your spec.

cards.heading: We buy pallets. We'll never build them.
cards.body: Steady recurring volume, paid on time, from a broker with no plant of its own to feed.

cards.heading: Freight on every order means we always need capacity.
cards.body: Regional lanes across the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic, moving pallets from mill to plant.

whoWeAre.heading: Built by people who were on the other side of the dock.
paragraphs: AGL started in North Canton, Ohio in January 2026, run by people who spent years buying pallets for manufacturers — living through capacity crunches, material shortages, and pricing whiplash from the receiving end. That's why the company is built the way it is.

ctaBand.heading: Let's talk about your pallet supply.
ctaBand.body: Send a spec and a quantity, or just call and describe the problem.
